used_documents.title: Fundamental rights in India
used_documents.text: The right to education at elementary level has been made one of the fundamental rights in 2002 under the Eighty - Sixth Amendment of 2002 . However this right was brought in to implementation after eight years in 2010 . Article 21A -- On 2 April 2010 , India joined a group of few countries in the world , with a historic law making education a fundamental right of every child coming into force . Making elementary education an entitlement for children in the 6 -- 14 age group , the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act will directly benefit children who do not go to school at present . This act provides for appointment of teachers with the requisite entry and academic qualifications .

India became one of 135 countries to make education a fundamental right of every child when the act came into force on 1 April 2010 . The title of the RTE Act incorporates the words ' free and compulsory ' . ' Free education ' means that no child , other than a child who has been admitted by his or her parents to a school which is not supported by the appropriate Government , shall be liable to pay any kind of fee or charges or expenses which may prevent him or her from pursuing and completing elementary education . used_documents.title: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
used_documents.text: The Act makes education a fundamental right of every child between the ages of 6 and 14 and specifies minimum norms in elementary schools . It requires all private schools ( except the minority institutions ) to reserve 25 % of seats for the poor and other categories of children ( to be reimbursed by the state as part of the public - private partnership plan ) . Children are admitted in to private schools based on caste - based reservations . See Page 9 and Point no 4 of This Document . It also prohibits all unrecognised schools from practice , and makes provisions for no donation or capitation fees and no interview of the child or parent for admission . The Act also provides that no child shall be held back , expelled , or required to pass a board examination until the completion of elementary education . There is also a provision for special training of school drop - outs to bring them up to par with students of the same age .

A.answer: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (RTE Act) provides for the right of children to free and compulsory education until completion of elementary education in a neighborhood school. It ensures that the appropriate government is obligated to provide free elementary education and compulsory admission, attendance, and completion of education for children aged 6 to 14. The Act also mandates that private schools reserve 25% of their seats for the poor and other categories of children, funded by the state through public-private partnerships. This act supports better quality education at the elementary level by ensuring free education and compulsory attendance, and by providing specific norms for elementary schools.

evidence.quote: The RTE Act provides for the right of children to free and compulsory education till completion of elementary education in a neighbourhood school . It clarifies that ' compulsory education ' means obligation of the appropriate government to provide free elementary education and ensure compulsory admission , attendance and completion of elementary education to every child in the six to fourteen age group . ' Free ' means that no child shall be liable to pay any kind of fee or charges or expenses which may prevent him or her from pursuing and completing elementary education .

The Act makes education a fundamental right of every child between the ages of 6 and 14 and specifies minimum norms in elementary schools . It requires all private schools ( except the minority institutions ) to reserve 25 % of seats for the poor and other categories of children ( to be reimbursed by the state as part of the public - private partnership plan ) . Children are admitted in to private schools based on caste - based reservations . See Page 9 and Point no 4 of This Document . It also prohibits all unrecognised schools from practice , and makes provisions for no donation or capitation fees and no interview of the child or parent for admission . The Act also provides that no child shall be held back , expelled , or required to pass a board examination until the completion of elementary education . There is also a provision for special training of school drop - outs to bring them up to par with students of the same age .

B.answer: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act (RTE), enacted in 2009 and implemented in 2010 [847772287_493-1860], ensures free elementary education for children aged 6 to 14 in a neighbourhood school [847772287_4120-4700]. To support better quality education, the Act specifies minimum norms in elementary schools [847772287_8764-9706] and mandates the appointment of teachers with requisite qualifications [809763888_36955-37663]. It requires private schools to reserve 25% of seats for poor categories, reimbursed by the state as part of a public-private partnership plan [847772287_17817-18365], a measure compared to school vouchers to address quality issues [847772287_17817-18365]. The Act also prohibits unrecognised schools, capitation fees, interviews, holding back children, or expulsion until completion of elementary education [847772287_8764-9706], and provides special training for school drop-outs to bring them up to par [847772287_8764-9706].

evidence.quote: The right to education at elementary level has been made one of the fundamental rights in 2002 under the Eighty - Sixth Amendment of 2002 . However this right was brought in to implementation after eight years in 2010 . Article 21A -- On 2 April 2010 , India joined a group of few countries in the world , with a historic law making education a fundamental right of every child coming into force . Making elementary education an entitlement for children in the 6 -- 14 age group , the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act will directly benefit children who do not go to school at present . This act provides for appointment of teachers with the requisite entry and academic qualifications .

The RTE Act provides for the right of children to free and compulsory education till completion of elementary education in a neighbourhood school . It clarifies that ' compulsory education ' means obligation of the appropriate government to provide free elementary education and ensure compulsory admission , attendance and completion of elementary education to every child in the six to fourteen age group . ' Free ' means that no child shall be liable to pay any kind of fee or charges or expenses which may prevent him or her from pursuing and completing elementary education .

To address these quality issues , the Act has provisions for compensating private schools for admission of children under the 25 % quota which has been compared to school vouchers , whereby parents may `` send '' their children in any school , private or public . This measure , along with the increase in PPP ( Public Private Partnership ) has been viewed by some organisations such as the All - India Forum for Right to Education ( AIF - RTE ) , as the state abdicating its `` constitutional obligation towards providing elementary education '' .

The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act or Right to Education Act ( RTE ) is an Act of the Parliament of India enacted on 4 August 2009 , which describes the modalities of the importance of free and compulsory education for children between the age of 6 to 14 years in India under Article 21A of the Indian Constitution . India became one of 135 countries to make education a fundamental right of every child when the act came into force on 1 April 2010 . The title of the RTE Act incorporates the words ' free and compulsory ' . ' Free education ' means that no child , other than a child who has been admitted by his or her parents to a school which is not supported by the appropriate Government , shall be liable to pay any kind of fee or charges or expenses which may prevent him or her from pursuing and completing elementary education . ' Compulsory education ' casts an obligation on the appropriate Government and local authorities to provide and ensure admission , attendance and completion of elementary education by all children in the 6 - 14 age group . With this , India has moved forward to a rights based framework that casts a legal obligation on the Central and State Governments to implement this fundamental child right as enshrined in the Article 21A of the Constitution , in accordance with the provisions of the RTE Act. 17 .

The Act makes education a fundamental right of every child between the ages of 6 and 14 and specifies minimum norms in elementary schools . It requires all private schools ( except the minority institutions ) to reserve 25 % of seats for the poor and other categories of children ( to be reimbursed by the state as part of the public - private partnership plan ) . Children are admitted in to private schools based on caste - based reservations . See Page 9 and Point no 4 of This Document . It also prohibits all unrecognised schools from practice , and makes provisions for no donation or capitation fees and no interview of the child or parent for admission . The Act also provides that no child shall be held back , expelled , or required to pass a board examination until the completion of elementary education . There is also a provision for special training of school drop - outs to bring them up to par with students of the same age .
